sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast. My name is Emili. I'm very happy you are here today.
In this episode, we will travel to Cairo, the capital of Egypt. Cairo is one of the oldest
and largest cities in the world. It is full of history, culture, and life. It is a place where
the ancient world and the modern world come together. Today, let's explore Cairo together in
slow and easy English. Are you ready? Let's begin. Part 1. Where is Cairo? Cairo is in Egypt,
in North Africa. It is the capital and the largest city of the country.
More than 20 million people live in the greater Cairo area. That makes it one of the biggest cities
in the world. Cairo is located near the Nile River, the longest river in the world. The river gives
life to the city and has been important for thousands of years. Part 2. The climate. Cairo has a desert
climate. This means it is hot and dry most of the year. Summer is very hot, with temperatures
often above 35 degrees Celsius. Winter is mild, with cooler nights but sunny days. Rain is very rare.
Because of the hot climate, many people go out in the evenings when it is cooler. Part 3.
A short history. Cairo has a very long and rich history. The area around Cairo has been important
for thousands of years. Not far from the city, you can see the great pyramids of Giza and the Sphinx.
These are more than 4,000 years old. Cairo itself was founded more than 1,000 years ago.
It became the capital of Egypt and a center for trade, culture, and learning.
Today, Cairo is a mix of old and new. You can see ancient monuments, Islamic architecture,
and modern skyscrapers in the same city. Part 4. The Nile River.
The Nile River is the heart of Cairo. It flows through the city and brings life to the desert.
Many people enjoy walking along the Nile. Taking boat rides or eating in restaurants by the water.
At night, the river shines with lights from the city. The Nile has always been important for Egypt.
From the time of the Pharaohs, until today. Part 5. Famous Landmarks.
Cairo is full of amazing landmarks. The pyramids of Giza. The most famous in the world built as
tombs for the Pharaohs. The Sphinx, a giant statue with the body of a lion and the face of a man.
The Egyptian Museum. It has thousands of treasures, including the golden mask of King Tutankhamen.
The Citadel of Cairo. A historic fortress with mosques and beautiful views of the city.
Al Azar Mosque. A famous mosque and one of the oldest universities in the world.
Each landmark shows a part of Cairo's rich story. Part 6. Daily Life in Cairo.
Cairo is a busy city. The streets are full of people, cars, and markets. The city never sleeps.
People in Cairo enjoy spending time with family and friends. They like to sit in cafes, drink tea,
and smoke shisha. In the evenings, the city is full of life, music, and lights.
Part 7. Egyptian Food. Cairo is a great place for food. Some popular dishes are
Koshari. A mix of rice, pasta, lentils, chickpeas, and tomato sauce.
Falafel. Fried balls made from beans. Usually eaten in bread. Full med-eams.
Cooked fava beans with oil and spices. Shawarma. Meat cooked on a spit. Served in bread with
vegetables and sauce. Baklava. A sweet dessert with pastry, nuts, and honey.
Street food is very popular in Cairo, and it is cheap and tasty.
Part 8. Culture and Religion. Cairo is the cultural heart of Egypt. It has music,
art, cinema, and theater. Egyptian Arabic is the most widely understood dialect in the
regular. Religion is also very important. Most people in Cairo are Muslim, but there are also
Christian communities. You can see many mosques and also historic churches.
Part 9. Markets and Shopping. Cairo is famous for its markets, called Suks.
The most famous is Khan El Khalili. Here you can buy spices, jewelry, perfumes, carpets, and souvenirs.
The market is full of colors, smells, and sounds. Modern shopping malls also exist in Cairo,
with international brands, so the city offers both traditional and modern shopping.
Part 10. Festivals and Celebrations. Cairo has many festivals. During Ramadan,
the city is full of lights and decorations. Families gather for big meals in the evening.
Eid al-Fita and Eid al-Adha are big celebrations with food and family.
Music and film festivals also happen in the city. These events show the joy and culture
of the people. Part 11. Education and Learning. Cairo is a center for education.
It has many universities, the most famous being Al Azar University, one of the oldest in the world.
The city is also home to libraries and cultural centers where people study and learn.
Part 12. Modern Life in Cairo. Cairo is growing fast. It has modern buildings, highways, and new
projects. But it also has problems like traffic and pollution, because so many people live there.
Still, the people of Cairo are friendly and welcoming. They are proud of their history
and happy to share their culture. Part 13. Why Visit Cairo? So why should you visit Cairo?
Because it has the pyramids and the sphinx, the Nile River, delicious food, busy markets,
and colorful life, history, culture, and traditions.
Warm and welcoming people. Cairo is a city where you can walk through thousands of years of history
in just one day. Outro. That is all for today's episode of the Slow English Podcast. We learned
about Cairo, the capital of Egypt. It is a city full of history, monuments, food, and life.
Slow English Podcast. I hope you enjoyed this journey and learn new words in English.
